prompt: In business terms, a tire producer is someone who
explanation: Makes things. Producers may be very creative, most of them do employ others, and they may sell their own products; however, the basic definition of a producer is someone that makes, or produces, things. Producers are growers, providers, or manufacturers of goods (e.g., tires) or services.

prompt: Selecting and obtaining goods and services to be resold at an auto parts store is called
explanation: Merchandising. Merchandising attempts to obtain items customers want to buy and to obtain appropriate quantities of those items so that they will be available when and where customers need them. Promotion communicates information about goods, services, images, and/or ideas to customers or clients to achieve a desired outcome. Operations deals with all the day-to-day functions of the business. Merchandising includes planning activities, but it is not called planning.

prompt: Which of the following is a component that is necessary for the production of goods and services in the automotive industry:
explanation: Natural resources. In order to produce goods and services, automotive businesses need a variety of resources. One type of resource is natural resources, which includes the materials from which to make products. Without the necessary raw materials and natural resources, many automotive businesses would be unable to produce goods and services. Tangible items are outputs produced by the production process. Purchasing plans are the procedures for buying needed materials. Research facilities are used to develop new products.

prompt: An auto-parts store that loses items to theft includes those items in the __________ category of a profit-and-loss statement.
explanation: Cost of goods sold. This element of the profit-and-loss statement includes all costs to obtain and/or produce the goods or services that an auto-parts store sells. Some of these costs include shoplifted or stolen items, because the store purchased those items even though they were not eventually available for sale due to theft. Operating expenses are all the expenses involved in running a store and are a separate category in a profit-and-loss statement. Capital goods are manufactured resources used to produce goods and services. Long-term liabilities are debts that will take longer than a year to pay. Capital goods and long-term liabilities are not separate categories in a profit-and-loss statement.

prompt: If all of the individuals who own a motorcycle parts business share unlimited liability for the business's losses, these individuals are part of a(n)
explanation: General partnership. With a general partnership, all partners are liable for the debts of the business. If one partner refuses to pay her/his share of the debts, the other partners will be responsible for paying them. Owners of close, public, and "S" corporations have limited liability.

prompt: Which of the following is a trend in vehicles and petroleum marketing that involves two or more businesses that share their skills, money, and distribution channels, while reducing costs:
explanation: Joint ventures. A joint venture is an arrangement that involves two or more businesses entering into a relationship by combining complementary resources, such as technology, skills, capital, or distribution channels, for the benefit of all parties. Joint ventures are a growing trend in vehicles and petroleum marketing because it allows two or more companies to share assets and often reduce costs. For example, several companies might form a joint venture to refine, transport, and sell petroleum products in a certain part of the world. A hostile takeover means that the company being acquired does not want to join with the other company. Two corporations combining to form one organization is a merger. A public buyout occurs when a public corporation buys back its stock and goes private.

prompt: One of the advantages of auto-parts store employees using word-processing software programs is that they usually contain a
explanation: Dictionary. Word-processing software programs are used to create text documents. An advantage of using these programs to write business letters, memos, reports, etc., is that the programs usually contain a dictionary that allows the user to check the spelling of words. The dictionary feature helps users to avoid making spelling mistakes in important business documents. Spreadsheet software programs have the capability of performing calculations. Graphics software programs allow users to create flowcharts.

prompt: When an automotive parts store employee searches the Web using a keyword and it returns 578 responses, the next logical step would be to
choices: start from #578 and work backwards until the best one is found.
go to another search engine and see if it works better.
open all 578 responses looking for the best one.
use more words for descriptors or a more precise keyword.
explanation: Use more words for descriptors or a more precise keyword. Unless the search engine will only allow one word to be used, it is better to use exact wording to get to the site that has the needed information. For example, using "automobile" as a keyword would very likely net several hundred or thousand sites, but if "muffler AND automobile AND Texas" is used, the search will be narrowed down tremendously. Opening all 578 responses is not practical. Starting at #578 is not effective because many search engines list the most popular sites related to the keyword first. Going to another search engine will probably net about the same number of results.

prompt: The use of technologically advanced on-board diagnostic systems in today's automobiles has impacted vehicle and petroleum marketing by requiring
explanation: Well-trained technicians. On-board diagnostic systems are controlled by sophisticated computers. These systems are complicated and require well-trained technicians who are able to identify problems and make needed repairs. The technologically advanced systems have made it almost impossible for untrained mechanics to work on modern automobiles. Today's automotive technicians need to understand the on-board diagnostic systems and read troubleshooting charts. Technology does not require computer-generated reports or high-speed distribution.

prompt: At the Jones Automobile Dealership, an employee needs to send an e-mail message to a coworker that he received from his supervisor. The most efficient way for the employee to communicate the information to his coworker is by
choices: posting the message in a secured e-mail folder.
sending the message by clicking on the reply box.
forwarding the message to the coworker's e-mail address.
printing the message and handing the copy to the coworker.
explanation: Forwarding the message to the coworker's e-mail address. Many automobile dealerships have e-mail systems that allow employees to communicate with each other. The e-mail forward option allows an e-mail message to be sent to e-mail users other than the sender. The reply option is used when the e-mail recipient responds to the message sender. Posting a message in a secured e-mail folder does not ensure that the coworker will read the message. Although the message can be printed and handed to the coworker, it is not the most efficient way to communicate the information.

prompt: One technique that many automotive parts stores use to prevent the shoplifting of expensive merchandise is by keeping those items in
explanation: Locked display cases. Keeping expensive merchandise in locked display cases is an effective way of preventing shoplifting. If customers want to examine the goods, they must ask a salesperson to open the case and show them the items. The salesperson stays with the customer and returns the items to the locked case if the customer decides not to buy. The opportunity for shoplifting has been eliminated. Keeping items in secure warehouses and distribution centers might prevent vendor or employee theft rather than shoplifting. Inexpensive impulse items are usually kept in shelves by cash registers.

prompt: Why is it important for oil-change shop employees to remain calm and try not to anger an armed robber?
choices: To reduce the risk of additional danger and serious injury
To avoid life endangerment and felonious assault lawsuits
So managers can quietly activate the silent alarm system
So law enforcement authorities have time to respond and surprise the assailant
explanation: To reduce the risk of additional danger and serious injury. The most important thing to do is to try to stay calm and not do anything that might anger the robber. By angering the robber, the event may escalate into a situation where someone gets hurt. If an alarm is on the premises, managers are not always around to activate it. Oil-change shop employees should be carefully trained to use the silent alarm system in the event of a robbery. If activating a silent alarm system while the robbery is occurring, employees should carefully follow the shop's procedures and policies. If an alarm is not activated, law enforcement authorities are not going to know about the robbery and will not respond to the situation. Robbery victims are not generally subject to prosecution or lawsuits.

prompt: When closing a tire and battery store for the night, what procedure do employees of a store often follow to make sure all customers have left?
explanation: Check the rest rooms. When closing a tire and battery store for the night, the employees should make sure that all customers have left. The purpose is to prevent anyone from hiding who plans to rob the store after the employees have closed for the night. One procedure to follow is to check the rest rooms and any other areas of the tire and battery store where customers might be. If they locate any customers, employees should politely tell them that the store is closing. After employees make sure all the customers have left, they turn off lights and lock the doors. Managers may view surveillance tapes if they suspect a customer of shoplifting.

prompt: Which of the following is a true statement about safety hazards in the vehicles and petroleum industry:
choices: Trial and error is a good way to learn use of tools and equipment.
Employees decide which protective clothing they should wear.
Personal habits can create safety hazards.
explanation: Personal habits can create safety hazards. Personal or family problems, stress, anger, fatigue, and alcohol and drug abuse can cause behavior problems that can lead to unsafe situations in vehicles and petroleum businesses. Keeping work areas clean and putting things away reduces the risk of injuries. Employees should not use tools and equipment without prior training because it can be hazardous to vehicles and petroleum workers who don't know how to use them properly. For their own safety, vehicles and petroleum employees should wear the appropriate clothing their employers designate.

prompt: Which of the following is not a guideline employees should follow when handling accidents in a automobile maintenance business:
choices: Make a full report of the accident.
explanation: Use CPR immediately. CPR is cardiopulmonary resuscitation, a technique used to restore breathing when an individual has stopped breathing. CPR would not be needed for all accident victims and should only be done by persons who have been trained in the proper techniques. Using basic first aid, calling for help if injuries are serious, and making a full report of the accident are all appropriate guidelines to follow.

prompt: One way for a muffler shop salesperson to effectively prepare for an oral presentation is to
explanation: Practice. Practicing is the best way for a muffler shop's salesperson to prepare for an oral presentation. There are several effective practicing techniques. Some people prefer to record their presentations and view them later in order to evaluate their performance. Others prefer to practice in front of a mirror or before a few coworkers in order to gain feedback. Whatever technique is used, practicing helps a muffler salesperson to become more comfortable and confident. The actual presentation involves articulating, communicating, and performing.

prompt: Joe, an employee with Tina's Tire Shop, must write a memo to his coworkers, which explains some new procedures. Which of the following is a guideline for writing clear instructions that Joe should use:
choices: Understand the process he is explaining
Confine the instructions to one page
explanation: Understand the process he is explaining. In order to write accurate instructions, Joe must be knowledgeable about the sequence and content of steps required for completion of the task. Instructions should consist of simple, brief statements which are written from the employee's (Joe's) perspective. Although instructions should be as brief as possible, the type and complexity of the process or activity will dictate the length of the instructions.

prompt: Which of the following information should be included in the inside address section of a business letter:
explanation: Title. The inside address section of a business letter should include the addressee's title, which might be both a courtesy title and a job title, if known. A courtesy title such as Mr. or Ms. should always be used and, whenever possible, a job title such as manager or president. A correct inside address with title is as follows: Mr. John Doe, President. The subject, date, and message are not part of the inside address section of a business letter.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of an automobile dealership employee behaving ethically when s/he provides personal information about a customer to another business:
choices: Notifying the customer after the fact
Sending the customer a copy of the information
explanation: Obtaining the customer's prior consent. Automobile dealership employees should behave ethically when processing and using a customer's personal information. One way for an automobile dealership employee to be ethical is to obtain the customer's prior consent before providing any personal information to another business. If the customer does not want certain information given to others, the automobile dealership employee is obligated to respect the customer's wishes. Under those circumstances, it would be unethical for the automobile dealership employee to share the personal information. It is not ethical for an automobile dealership employee to give the information to others and then notify the customer or to send the customer a copy of the information that the business shares. It is unethical for businesses to sell customers' personal information without their permission.

prompt: In the automotive industry, moving or transferring the ownership of goods or services are __________ activities.
explanation: Distribution. Distribution involves moving, storing, locating, and/or transferring ownership of goods and services. Distribution activities serve as the link between and among automotive businesses by enabling goods to be moved from one place to another where they are needed. Selling is responding to consumer needs and wants through planned, personalized communications in order to influence purchase decisions and enhance future business opportunities. Shipping is one method of transportation. Transportation is the method used for moving goods from place to place.

prompt: Technological advancements have made it possible for some vehicles and petroleum businesses to communicate directly with customers, which reduces the need to use
explanation: Intermediaries. Intermediaries are distribution channel members operating between the producer and the consumer or industrial users to help in the movement of goods and services. In some cases, it is possible for a customer to order products (e.g., automotive) directly from a business's web site rather than going through a distributor or traditional retail outlet. Technological advancements do not necessarily reduce the need for raw materials. Vehicles and petroleum businesses use raw materials to produce goods. Technological advancements have not necessarily reduced the need to use warehouse personnel and freight carriers in relation to communicating with customers.

prompt: If an auto-parts wholesaler objects to a supplier's policies restricting trade or competition, it is illegal for the supplier to __________ with the wholesaler.
explanation: Refuse to deal. It is illegal for a supplier to refuse to deal with a channel member in an existing distribution channel solely because the channel member disagrees with a policy that may be illegal in itself (i.e., restricts trade or limits competition). Suppliers routinely communicate and do business with wholesalers, but not doing so is not illegal. Suppliers usually try to comply with a wholesaler's requests.

prompt: In which of the following situations would an auto-parts store employee need to know the identification number of a part:
choices: To identify the correct installation tool
To locate a replacement in inventory
explanation: To locate a replacement in inventory. Replacement parts vary from one car to another, and in many cases, similar parts are not compatible. To be able to locate the correct replacement part in the inventory, an auto-parts store employee needs to know the identification number of the part. Each part contains a specific number that identifies it from other similar parts. This number allows the employee to locate the part that is designed for use in a specific model of each automobile. Auto-parts store employees do not complete the repair work or assemble components. Although parts are slightly different for various models of cars, the tools needed to install the part are usually the same.

prompt: The official record of the arrival of a shipment of merchandise at an auto-parts store is found in the
explanation: Receiving log. The receiving log is a receiving record used to list, or log, all data about a shipment of goods. Each shipment is recorded on a single line with a printed number, and that number is assigned to the shipment as its receiving number. A purchase order is a form that auto-parts stores use to order goods. An invoice is the shipper's bill for goods sent to the purchaser. A discrepancy report is used by some auto-parts stores to describe items missing from an order.

prompt: What should an auto parts store's receiving employees do if they find that a carton of automobile air filters have been crushed and severely damaged during shipment?
choices: File a claim with the carrier
Return the carton to the supplier
explanation: File a claim with the carrier. Goods that are damaged during shipment are the responsibility of the carrier. The automotive parts store should file a claim with the carrier in order to be reimbursed for the cost of the automobile air filters. The automotive parts store might order an additional carton at a later time, but the first action is to file a claim. The carrier might instruct the automotive parts store to destroy the damaged goods or keep them until the claim is settled. The automotive parts store would not return the damaged carton to the supplier.

prompt: An auto-parts warehouse employee who selects three batteries, five sets of windshield wipers, and four sets of floor mats to send to a customer is
explanation: Fulfilling an order. Auto-parts warehouse employees routinely fulfill orders by selecting from inventory the items that customers have ordered. In many cases, the employee walks through the warehouse and selects the various items from the shelves or storage racks. This is a labor-intensive process, but often the only way to fulfill an order for a certain number of specific items. The employee who selects certain items to send to a customer is not checking the inventory or measuring the stockturn. Once the employee has selected the items, s/he might package them to ship to a customer.

prompt: When routing auto-parts stock from storage to the sales floor, most retailers send the goods that
explanation: Were received first. Most retailers want to sell old merchandise before they sell new goods. As a result, they rotate auto-parts stock from storage to the sales floor according to which goods were received first. For example, items received in March would be routed to the sales floor before the items that were received in May. If stores don't sell the older goods first, they run the risk of accumulating items that customers will not buy because new items are on the shelf. Stores do not route stock to the sales floor according to which items are the most expensive, appeal to many customers, or have a high markup.

prompt: Which of the following might result if tire and battery shop employees fail to maintain adequate inventory levels:
explanation: Lost sales. A tire and battery shop that fails to maintain adequate inventory levels may not have the products in stock that customers want, which may result in lost sales. Losing potential sales is costly to the tire and battery shop because dissatisfied customers might not return, and profits might decrease. Failing to maintain adequate inventory levels does not result in lower prices or higher costs.

prompt: A muffler shop has opening stock value of $23,500, stock purchases of $6,250, net sales transactions of $24,675, and periodic stock count of $4,860. What is the shop's dollar amount of inventory shrinkage?
explanation: $215. To calculate the muffler shop's dollar amount of inventory shrinkage, begin with the dollar figure from the previous physical count and add the purchases made since that count was taken ($23,500 + $6,250 = $29,750). This will show the total dollar value of inventory that should be on hand. Then, subtract the total sales transactions from this figure ($29,750 - $24,675 = $5,075). Subtract the periodic stock count from the perpetual inventory, the amount that should be on hand, to determine inventory shrinkage ($5,075 - $4,860 = $215).

prompt: In order to accurately maintain a unit inventory control system, an automotive parts store's employees should periodically
explanation: Count stock. Automotive parts businesses should manually count the stock periodically in order to make sure that the actual count matches the amount indicated in the unit inventory control system. If discrepancies are found during the stock counting process, then the information in the inventory control system should be revised. Discrepancies may occur if some goods have been stolen or damaged and discarded. These changes should be made to the inventory control system in order to accurately maintain the system. In order to accurately maintain a unit inventory control system, automotive parts businesses would not alter forms, define data, or total sales.

prompt: "Economic votes" are cast by consumers each time they
explanation: Make a purchase. When consumers make purchases, they are voting for those products and against others which they did not buy. This influences which products will be produced and at what price they will be sold. Market research uses surveys, interviews, and other methods to identify consumers and their buying habits. Consumers who visit a business without making purchases do not provide the business with any information.

prompt: The quantity of products that buyers are ready to purchase at a given time at a given price is
explanation: Demand. Demand is affected by increases and decreases in price. Stock is the inventory maintained by a business. Supply is the quantity of a good or service that sellers are able and willing to offer for sale at a specified price in a given time period. Quality refers to the degree of excellence of a good/service.

prompt: Any price below the equilibrium price will generally result in
explanation: Excess demand. Excess demand is the situation that exists when demand is greater than supply. When prices are lower, consumers usually purchase more goods and services, thereby increasing demand. Excess supply is the situation that exists when supply is greater than demand. Rationing is a function of relative prices that determines who gets the goods and services produced. Competition is the rivalry between two or more businesses to attract scarce customer dollars.

prompt: Auto-parts stores must be careful about increasing the prices of their goods in order to increase profits because the result may be that they
explanation: Lose sales to competitors. If competitors sell the same goods at lower prices, customers may switch to them. The loss of sales may wipe out any increase in profits from the higher prices. Stockholders may influence a corporation's pricing policy, but they are not likely to change their investment because of increased prices. Also, not all auto-parts stores are structured as corporations and therefore, do not have stockholders. Increasing prices would not increase operating expenses or cause the auto-parts stores to need new suppliers.

prompt: When the climate is the primary factor affecting available jobs, this is an example of specialization of labor according to
explanation: Natural resources. Some jobs depend on certain climatic conditions, or the availability of natural resources. Specialization by stages of production occurs when more than one stage is required to change a raw material into a finished product. Specialization of human resources occurs when people use their different skills and abilities in jobs for which they are best suited. The most common type of specialization of human resources is by trade or profession, the type of work you perform in order to earn a living.

prompt: Which of the following represents the principal goal of organized labor in the United States:
explanation: Collective bargaining. Collective bargaining is the negotiating process in which union officials and company representatives engage to determine the terms and conditions that are to be provided employees. An individual goal of collective bargaining might be to increase worker influence in decision making. Increasing management influence and eliminating government control are not desired by organized labor.

prompt: Based on the information in the following chart, determine the point at which the law of diminishing returns begins to take effect: Number of Workers Units of Products Produced 1 12 2 26 3 40 4 48 5 54 6 58
explanation: Four workers. The law of diminishing returns states that, at some point, continuing to add workers will reduce overall productivity. This occurs because there is a limited amount of other variables such as work space and raw materials. In the chart, the law of diminishing returns begins to take effect when the fourth worker is hired. Production increased by 14 with the addition of the second worker, and again by 14 with the addition of the third worker. However, the addition of the fourth worker only increased production by 8, which is the beginning of the decline. Adding the fifth and sixth workers created an even greater decline in productivity.

prompt: One of the reasons an auto-parts shop allows customers to use credit is because it provides
explanation: Convenience. Credit allows an auto-parts shop's customers to pay for several different purchases at one time with a single payment. It reduces the need to carry cash and provides the convenience of ordering by telephone or by the Internet. Collateral is anything of value belonging to the borrower which is pledged to the lender to guarantee that the loan will be repaid. Interest is the fee which lenders charge borrowers for the use of credit. Credit does not provide reassurance or comfort.

prompt: What is a benefit of marketing research?
choices: Provides data for a specific situation
Takes the place of data analysis
Increases the cost of goods and services
explanation: Provides data for a specific situation. Marketing research is the systematic gathering, recording, and analyzing of data about a specific problem. Such data may be needed when the data in the marketing-information management system do not apply to the circumstances or are insufficient. The data that are gathered must still be analyzed in order to be useful to the business. Marketing-research activities may increase the cost of goods and services, and that is a disadvantage rather than a benefit. Marketing research does not necessarily create fair competition, but it may help the business to be competitive.

prompt: What is the device that an auto-parts store's employees use to obtain information about customers who access their web sites?
explanation: Cookies. Some web-site computers place information, a "cookie," on a user's hard drive when the user visits the site. The next time a user visits that site, the site's computer recognizes the user because of the cookie. Marketing-information employees use cookies to maintain user information and track how many times a user visits a specific web site or buys a product. This type of data allows marketing-information employees to customize web sites in order to appeal to the preferences and habits of the consumers who are visiting their sites. A browser is software that allows a computer to access information on the Internet. Spiders are a type of search tool. A bookmark is a term used to describe a web site that is marked for later reference.

prompt: Automobile dealerships often maintain current demographic information to make decisions about the most effective strategy to use to
explanation: Reach the target market. Demographic information is information about the physical and social characteristics of the population such as age, marital status, income, etc. Automobile dealerships often maintain current demographic information to make decisions about the most effective strategy to use to reach the target market, which is the particular group of customers the automobile dealership seeks to attract. By monitoring demographic information, automobile dealerships are able to detect changes in the target market and revise the marketing strategy to remain effective. Demographic information does not help automobile dealerships to make decisions about the most effective strategy to use to analyze the economy, negotiate with suppliers, or purchase new equipment.

prompt: Carl's Auto Body Shop needs more information in order to define the reason for its research and to decide which direction to take. What type of marketing research would employees use?
explanation: Exploratory. Exploratory research collects information to help Carl's Auto Body Shop employees define its issue, situation, or concern and decide which direction to go in order to address it. Descriptive research is used to gather specific information that is related to the identified issue, situation, or concern. Causal research focuses on cause and effect and tests "what if" theories. Predictive research is used to help the business forecast future business developments.

prompt: What process do automobile repair employees follow after collecting marketing research in order to make it useful?
explanation: Analyzing. Once an automobile repair business collects marketing information, it must analyze the data in order to make it useful. First, the automobile repair business tabulates or codes the information into a specific format or category. Then, the automobile repair business is able to evaluate or analyze the information and use it to answer the particular issue or problem being researched. For example, if an automobile repair business collects one hundred questionnaires from customers, it would need to analyze the information on the questionnaires before it could use the data. Sampling is a technique for obtaining marketing information. The results of the research are reported after the information is collected and analyzed. Automobile repair businesses often store marketing information in the event that it will be useful at a later date.

prompt: Marketing strategies help vehicles and petroleum businesses to achieve their goals by providing the businesses with marketing
explanation: Plans. In order to be successful, automobile and petroleum businesses must have goals they want to attain and strategies, or plans, to meet those goals. These plans must be analyzed and evaluated constantly in order to meet the ever-changing needs of consumers. Profits are the monies retained by the vehicles and petroleum businesses, and they are major incentives for developing viable strategies. Technology is scientific applications to business objectives or the methods used to attain those objectives.

prompt: What types of environmental factors do oil companies often consider when conducting a situational analysis?
explanation: Internal and external. The environmental factors that oil companies consider when conducting a situational analysis may be internal as well as external. Internal factors are those within the oil company itself that have an impact on the business's marketing effort, such as the distribution system or the pricing strategy. External factors are those that exist outside the oil company and over which the business may have no control, such as the state of the economy or the number of competitors. Oil companies examine both types of environmental factors in order to adapt to change and make effective marketing decisions. For example, an oil company might decide to adjust its prices to remain competitive in the marketplace. Physical and personal, ethical and legal, and formal and informal are not types of environmental factors that businesses consider when conducting a situational analysis.

prompt: Why do automotive businesses develop marketing plans?
explanation: To attract the target customer. A marketing plan is a set of procedures or strategies for attracting the target customer to an automotive business. The target market is the group of people identified and selected as the primary users of a product. Each automotive business has a specific target market and develops a marketing plan for the purpose of reaching that market. Providing quality service and expanding the distribution system are marketing strategies that an automotive business might use to attract the target customer. Automotive businesses do not develop marketing plans for the purpose of preparing revenue statements.

prompt: An auto body repair shop's personnel needs are ultimately determined by the business's
explanation: Sales. An auto body repair shop whose sales are expected to increase knows it may need more workers, while an auto body repair shop whose sales are expected to decline or to remain the same will not need more workers. An auto body repair shop's promotional mix is based on media's ability to reach the targeted audience. Decisions about finance and purchases are all based on anticipated sales.

prompt: Team members should try to keep their emotions under control because that will
explanation: Help them to be objective. Controlling feelings helps people to have an objective point of view. It also keeps feelings or attitudes from getting in the way of decision-making. Controlling feelings does not prevent anger but controls the way anger is expressed. It also does not improve morale or maintain an informal atmosphere.

prompt: An automobile dealership employee tried to look at a problem from a customer's point of view. Which of the following was the employee practicing:
explanation: Empathy. Empathy is the ability to put yourself in another person's place. Empathy forms a bond between sender and receiver, allowing easier communication to take place. Passivity is a lack of response to what is being said. Prejudice is a negative prejudgment that is not based on reason and is a block to effective communication. Inattention means a lack of attention.

prompt: What type of plan do auto-parts store employees use when an original plan cannot be carried out?
explanation: Back-up. A back-up plan is often known as "Plan B," or the contingency plan in the event that the original plan will not work for some reason. Auto-parts stores often develop back-up plans in order to be prepared for the unexpected. There's no way to know when a crisis will occur, such as helping customers when the store's power goes out, so having a contingency plan often helps an auto-parts store to be successful even under adverse conditions. Marketing plans are the blueprint for an auto-parts store's marketing activities and financial plans provide details about an auto-parts store's financial (money) needs and status. New-supplemental is not a term that most auto-parts stores use to describe a back-up plan.

prompt: Automotive businesses whose employees help to control expenses often experience savings that they may pass on to
explanation: Customers. Automotive businesses often save money when their employees help to control expenses. Many automotive businesses pass on these savings to customers by offering lower prices or regular discounts which might encourage them to frequent the business. Automotive businesses do not pass on savings to suppliers, creditors, or advertisers although they might use some of the savings to pay off bills or loans, or purchase additional advertising to attract more customers.

prompt: The relationship between recreation and good health is that recreation is
explanation: Essential to good health. Recreational activities help us to get away from life's frustrations and tensions and to relax. It is beneficial to mental, physical, and emotional health when people regularly enjoy some form of recreation. Recreation is not a luxury and may be as simple as taking a walk.

prompt: Which of the following statements does not reflect a person's integrity:
choices: I am truthful in all situations.
I don't take anything that isn't mine.
I pay all my debts promptly.
I listen in on others' conversations.
explanation: I listen in on others' conversations. Individuals who have integrity adhere to an established set of personal ethics and sound moral principles. This means that they avoid eavesdropping on other people's conversations. Being truthful, not taking others' property, and paying bills promptly all demonstrate integrity.

prompt: Which of the following is a true statement regarding initiative:
choices: People with initiative must usually be prodded into doing things.
Possessing initiative is unimportant in marketing occupations.
Increased initiative usually brings increased job responsibility.
Initiative should be demonstrated only at your place of employment.
explanation: Increased initiative usually brings increased job responsibility. Increased job responsibility is just one benefit of demonstrating initiative. If you possess initiative, you are ready, willing, and able to both think and act on your own. You do not have to be prodded or urged to do so. Initiative is extremely important to workers in all types of occupations, especially in the field of marketing. In order to be viewed as a person with initiative, your willingness to think and act on your own should be reflected in all areas of your life.

prompt: People with high self-esteem are usually __________ at learning new skills.
explanation: Good. One of the benefits of a high level of self-esteem is that it helps people to learn new skills more easily because they have the necessary confidence in their abilities.

prompt: Meaningful goals can give you a sense of __________ in your life.
explanation: Direction. Goals are objectives that people want to fulfill. Having meaningful goals can point you in a specific direction and also help to keep you on target. Generally, having goals tends to reduce feelings of insecurity and uncertainty. Goals must be achieved in order to give you a sense of accomplishment.

prompt: Which of the following is a source of career information that is available in most schools:
explanation: Guidance counselor. Most schools have guidance counselors on staff who help students obtain career information and give them advice about possible occupations. Guidance counselors maintain current information about various types of jobs and can help students locate information that is not available at school. Guidance counselors often keep in touch with local employers and provide students with information about current job openings in the community. Industry recruiters may visit schools occasionally to recruit for specific occupations. The school's admissions director and curriculum planner are not sources of career information.

prompt: What question is often asked in the work experience section of an employment application?
choices: Eligibility to work in this country
explanation: Reason for leaving previous job. Most employment applications ask why you left previous jobs. The answer should be positive and not in any way critical of a former employer. Common reasons for leaving previous jobs include accepting a better position, returning to school, or because the job was a seasonal position that ended. The question about eligibility to work in this country usually appears in the personal information section. Questions about course of study completed are contained in the education section. The question about availability to begin work is usually in a general section about type of job desired.

prompt: When automobile manufacturers increase the quality of materials used in the production of their products, their prices will tend to be
explanation: Higher. Automobile manufacturers that use high-quality materials in the production of their goods have to pay higher prices for the materials. They will pass these increased costs on to their customers, so prices do not stay the same. The prices are not usually reduced (lowered).

prompt: Which of the following is a procedure developed by advances in technology that many auto parts stores are using to attach prices to products:
explanation: Electronic marking. Electronic marking is a procedure that allows auto parts stores to use a device to code prices onto tags or tickets. These electronically marked prices can be read and processed by optical scanners at checkout counters. The price information then is transmitted through the auto-parts store's computer system which automatically deletes the product from inventory. The electronic marking system allows auto-parts stores to maintain accurate information about the product. Optical scanning is a method of reading prices that are marked electronically. Magnetic transferring and digital processing are not ways of attaching prices to products.

prompt: Several offshore oil rigs were severely damaged by hurricanes this year. The selling price of a gallon of gasoline has been set 50¢ higher this year than last. Which of the following factors affected the price of gasoline:
explanation: Supply and demand. When the supply of a product is less than the demand, marketers often increase the selling price. Production costs, competition, and product life cycle are not factors that caused the selling price to increase in this situation.

prompt: Which of the following is the purpose of screening ideas for new products:
choices: To perform a thorough business analysis
explanation: To eliminate some ideas. Screening ideas for new products is intended to eliminate obviously bad ideas and recognize the value of good ideas. It is a quick look at ideas to see if they have value, not a careful or thorough analysis. New ideas must already be generated before screening can occur. Market research would be done to determine if consumers will purchase the good or service.

prompt: The product life-cycle stage in which competitors are most likely to enter the market is
explanation: Growth. By the time a product reaches the growth stage, its sales are rising rapidly, and competitors rush to get a share of the market. Competition reaches its peak and levels off in the maturity stage. Competition is at low levels in both the introductory and decline stages of the life cycle because competitors are either waiting to see how the new product sells or not interested in competing for market share of a product that is on its way out.

prompt: One reason gasoline and diesel fuels are graded according to uniform standards is to allow consumers to select the fuel that is
choices: readily available at most service stations.
best suited for their vehicles' engines.
explanation: Best suited for their vehicles' engines. Gasoline and diesel fuels are graded according to uniform standards because certain fuels work better in certain types of engines. For example, there is a difference between engines that run on gasoline and those that run on diesel fuel. Also, there are differences between the various engines within those two categories. Some automobile engines need a premium grade of gasoline, while others run smoothly on regular. The grading system makes it easy for consumers to select the gasoline or diesel fuel that is best suited for their vehicles' engines. Although some fuels are more effective in cold weather, that is not the reason for the grading system. The grading system does not allow consumers to select the fuel that is the least expensive or readily available.

prompt: An auto-parts company advertises that a product it makes comes with a 15-year warranty guaranteeing full replacement, if the item is damaged in floods or storms. The company is using the warranty mainly
explanation: As a promotional tool. Businesses use warranties or guarantees in their advertising as a promotional tool to help gain new customers. Advertising a 15-year warranty guaranteeing full replacement is a good way to promote the sale of a product to prospective customers who may be purchasing the item. Businesses often use a warranty as a competitive tool when competing with foreign producers. A business that satisfactorily handles a customer's problem with a warranted product often gains repeat customers. Warranties protect sellers because they clearly define the seller's responsibilities to consumers.

prompt: When buying a new car that has a new-vehicle warranty, why might a customer not wish to buy the extended service contract?
choices: Extended service contracts are usually comprehensive.
Coverage is substantially less than manufacturers' warranties.
Coverage for preexisting conditions is included.
Benefits of the contract run simultaneously with manufacturers' warranties.
explanation: Coverage is substantially less than manufacturers' warranties. Extended service contracts provide coverage that is substantially less than manufacturer's warranties at a far greater price. Coverage for preexisting conditions is not included and there are complicated procedures for obtaining approval for covered repairs. These contracts are not comprehensive, unlike manufacturer's warranties. Benefits of the contract do not become effective until the manufacturer's warranty expires.

prompt: Which of the following safeguards consumers by preventing automobile businesses from using false and deceptive advertisements:
explanation: Federal Trade Commission Act. This act was passed in 1914 and established the Federal Trade Commission, which administers laws that forbid false, misleading, or deceptive advertising of consumer products. The Sherman Antitrust Act is intended to prevent monopolies and price fixing. The Robinson-Patman Act forbids businesses (e.g., automobile) from discriminating in the prices or services offered to competing customers. The Clayton Act is intended to prevent specific business actions that might prohibit competition.

prompt: When the Lightning Fast Oil Change chain makes changes in the type and amount of services it offers, it is making strategy changes in its
explanation: Product mix. The product mix includes all the different goods and services that the Lightning Fast Oil Change chain sells. A product line is a group of closely related products manufactured or sold by a business. Promotional mix is the combination of the different types of promotion a business uses. A product item is a specific model or brand of a product.

prompt: If no purchases have been committed prior to the start of the month, at that point, planned purchases and open-to-buy are
explanation: Equal. Open-to-buy is the difference between planned purchases and the purchase commitments already made by a buyer for a given time period, which is usually a month. This represents the amount the buyer has left to spend for that month. The amount is reduced each time a purchase is made. Therefore, at the start of the month, if no purchases have been committed, planned purchases and open-to-buy are equal; they are not disproportionate. Planned purchases and open-to-buy cannot both increase because as purchases are made, open-to-buy must decrease. Planned purchases and open-to-buy, by their very nature, are known to buyers.

prompt: When the airbag was a new product in the automobile industry, what strategy was most likely used to initially position it in the marketplace?
explanation: Benefits. One way automobile companies position their goods and services in the marketplace is by emphasizing product benefits. Automobile marketers emphasize how the product is different from other similar products. When airbags were initially developed and available for installation in some automobiles, they provided drivers of the cars with additional injury protection if an accident occurred. Therefore, emphasis was placed on the benefits (e.g., protection, safety) of having the airbag in the automobile. A new product in the marketplace would not initially experience competition. Price would not likely be used to position the product because product development is very expensive. The product might be more expensive when it is introduced in the marketplace to cover development costs and because there is no competition. Although quality is often an important consideration, the first airbag in the marketplace did not have similar products in which its quality could be compared.

prompt: A well-known car manufacturer sells the right to use its logo to another company to use on a variety of specialty items. This is an example of brand
explanation: Licensing. Licensing allows a brand name to be used by another company for a fee. Brand positioning attempts to create a certain image or impression of a brand as compared to competitive brands. Brand extension is the use of successful brands to launch new brands. Brand repositioning reevaluates and changes the brand in order to change the ways consumers see the brand.

prompt: Calculate the dollar amount of planned reductions if estimated sales for next month are $74,000, planned shortages are 3%, and planned discounts are 2.5%.
explanation: $4,070. Shortages and discounts are types of reductions. A business estimates the percentage of these reductions in order to calculate their dollar value. The business adds the two percentages to arrive at total reductions of 5.5% (3% + 2.5% = 5.5%). Then the business multiplies the amount of planned sales by the total percentage of planned reductions ($74,000 x 5.5% = $4,070). The planned reductions in dollars amount to $4,070.

prompt: For most automotive businesses, the ultimate goal of using promotion is to
explanation: Sell goods or services. The major purpose of using promotion for most automotive businesses is to increase their sales. Promotion helps to do this by informing, reminding, and persuading customers. Promotion is also used to introduce new products and to attract customers to an automotive business. Consumer demand can be created but not controlled.

prompt: A type of promotion that aims to persuade consumers to buy a specific good or service is __________ promotion.
explanation: Product. Product promotion is used to stimulate consumer purchases of goods or services. Primary product promotion aims to stimulate demand for an entire class of goods or services. Secondary product promotion is used to stimulate demand for a specific brand of a product. Institutional promotion is used to create a certain image of the company in the eyes of the consumer.

prompt: Free samples, sweepstakes, contests, coupons, demonstrations, and trade shows are examples of
explanation: Sales promotion. Sales promotion is promotional activities other than advertising, personal selling, and publicity which marketers use to stimulate consumer demand. Publicity is any nonpersonal presentation of ideas, goods, or services that is not paid for by the company which receives it. Advertising is a paid form of nonpersonal presentation of ideas, goods, or services. Personal selling uses planned, personalized communication in order to influence purchase decisions.

prompt: An automobile dealership wants to promote products to a large audience by using electronic display panels. Which of the following is the most likely medium that the dealership would use:
explanation: Baseball stadium. Large arenas or stadiums that attract thousands of people to a sporting or entertainment event often house electronic display panels. The panels can be used for fans to keep score during a sporting event, view entertainers during a performance, and advertise a wide assortment of products that range from automobiles to soft drinks. Parking meters and transit shelters are examples of outdoor advertising formats. Parking meters and transit shelters often display advertisements in a printed (e.g. poster) form. In addition, the audience for these media is limited. Airplane hangers are storage units for aircraft. Electronic display panels are often found in airport terminals where thousands of people pass through them each day.

prompt: What element of a print advertisement is often considered to be as important as the headline for attracting attention?
explanation: Illustration. An illustration is a photograph, drawing, painting, or graphic such as a chart, table, or graph. The illustration often is considered to be as important as the headline for attracting attention and arousing interest. Sometimes it is more important because it is noticed first. The illustration also can create desire by showing the product and/or its uses and benefits. Logotype or signature is the name and/or symbol used by a business. Identification is the element of an advertisement that identifies the product or the advertiser and may include additional information about the business.

prompt: Which of the following statements is true regarding direct advertising strategies:
choices: Telemarketing programs are generally considered to be obsolete forms of direct advertising.
Use of e-mail advertising messages rewards most marketers with a very high response rate.
Marketers often select their direct advertising methods based on consumers' preferences.
Infomercial and home shopping television are the least effective media to send promotional messages.
explanation: Marketers often select their direct advertising methods based on consumers' preferences. Customers often respond to promotional messages for certain products when those messages are transmitted via direct advertising (e.g., direct mail) rather than other media. For example, research indicates that customers generally prefer to receive information regarding grocery, health, and beauty products through direct mail rather than through other venues such as telephone or in retail establishments. Although direct advertising often rewards businesses with higher response rates than other forms of advertising, it cannot be assumed that most businesses receive high response rates. Computer messages (e.g., spam) are often deleted by users before the message is opened, which lowers response rates. Although some governments have introduced legislation to restrict telemarketing programs, the media is not necessarily becoming obsolete. Infomercial and home shopping television shows can be very effective promotional tools that often experience immediate response from customers.

prompt: What is the database that allows an auto-parts business to deal efficiently with very large amounts of data by linking the tables where data is stored?
explanation: Relational. A relational database-management system eliminates the need for storing the same information in several places by using codes to link tables together. A flat-file database is one that cannot be linked, such as a spreadsheet. A customized database is one that has been altered to meet an auto parts business's exact needs. File Maker is a brand name.

prompt: One way that auto-parts stores maintain their displays is by making sure that the displays contain
explanation: Abundant product. Maintaining displays involves making sure that the displays contain abundant product. Auto-parts stores often add product to displays because customers remove items throughout the day. Displays that contain a small amount of product often appear unattractive and disorganized to customers. Also, customers may think that the items have been on display too long if they are in disarray and limited in number. Not all store displays contain seasonal goods, nonperishable items, or similar merchandise.

prompt: Automotive accessory stores often set up point-of-sale displays near the checkout counter to promote the sale of
explanation: Seasonal merchandise. Point-of-sale displays are often used to promote the sale of additional products or seasonal merchandise that the automotive accessory store does not regularly stock. Point-of-sale displays are frequently provided by a vendor and are self-contained units stocked with merchandise. Stores often set up these displays near the checkout counter to remind customers of the seasonal goods. Customers often pick up these goods while they are waiting to pay. Most stores do not set up displays near checkout counters to promote the sale of expensive items. Traditional products and staple goods are the routine items that the store carries on a regular basis. These items usually are stocked on shelves rather than in point-of-sale displays.

prompt: The component of the promotional plan that determines the funds available for promotion is the promotional
explanation: Budget. The promotional budget establishes the amount of money that the business plans to spend on its promotional efforts. There are a number of ways the business can determine how much to allocate to promotion. One method is to base the promotional budget on the firm's expected sales and adjust it during the year if sales are higher or lower than expected. The promotional mix is the combination, or blend, of marketing communication channels that a business uses to send its messages to consumers. The promotional method is the particular medium or media chosen to deliver the promotional message. The promotional objectives are the goals the firm wishes to achieve through its promotional efforts.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of coordinating an automotive accessory store's promotional activities:
choices: Printing coupons in a suburban newspaper
Using personal selling to increase the customer's total purchase
Suggesting that the customer trade up to a more expensive product
Advertising a new product and giving customers samples of the product
explanation: Advertising a new product and giving customers samples of the product. This is an example of coordinating advertising and sales promotion, two types of promotional activities, because they are being used together to market the product. Advertising brings customers to the business, and sales promotion techniques such as giving customers samples help to persuade them to buy. Providing coupons and using personal selling are promotional activities, but they are being used alone rather than as part of a coordinated effort. Suggesting that a customer trade up is not a promotional activity.

prompt: Tim goes to the auto-parts store to buy windshield wipers but realizes that he isn't sure what type of wipers he needs. The clerk says that if the wipers are the wrong size, he can exchange them for the correct size. The store is building a loyal clientele by offering
explanation: Favorable adjustment and return policies. The clerk informs Tim that he can come back and get the right windshield wipers if the ones that he purchases are not what he needs. The hardware store is offering a liberal return policy which creates an environment that helps to build customer loyalty. Quality maintenance and repair services involve a company providing good services to back up its product. Readily available credit refers to a store providing credit, which may be needed for the sale of more expensive goods. Assistance with merchandising refers to the company and salesperson assisting with merchandising the product, such as helping with sales promotion ideas and/or point-of-purchase displays.

prompt: Salespeople who moonlight or attend classes on company time are guilty of
explanation: Unethical behavior. Unethical behavior involves acting in a way that is wrong. Salespeople who moonlight or attend classes on company time are behaving unethically because they are not working during the time for which they are being paid. They are, in effect, stealing from the business. Some businesses may allow employees to hold second jobs but only on their own time and if it does not interfere with their performance. Businesses usually expect employees to attend class on their own time. Misusing company assets involves using company cars for personal activities or padding expense accounts. Salespeople who moonlight or attend classes on company time are not wasting their time but are using company time for personal activities. Moonlighting or attending classes on company time are not violations of the law.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of price discrimination:
choices: Buying products from one company that are available for a lower price from another company
Offering substantial discounts to buyers of large quantities of a certain product
Asking a company for a price break on products at the end of the regular season
Selling the same quantity of the same product to different customers for different prices
explanation: Selling the same quantity of the same product to different customers for different prices. This is an example of price discrimination and is often considered an illegal selling activity. If a business charges different customers different prices for similar amounts and types of products, it is involved in price discrimination, which is a violation of certain selling regulations. Customers often ask companies for price breaks on products at the end of the regular season. It is legal to offer substantial discounts to buyers of large quantities of certain products and to buy products from one company that are available for a lower price from another company.

prompt: Which of the following is a technique that automobile salespeople can use to obtain selling information from company promotional materials:
explanation: Read newspaper ads. Many automobile businesses (e.g., dealerships) routinely advertise their goods and services in local newspapers. These advertisements generally contain important information, such as price, discounts, delivery, warranty, or rebates, that would help salespeople to sell the product to customers. Reading newspaper ads keeps salespeople informed and helps them perform their job. Attending seminars, talking with managers, and visiting libraries are other ways of obtaining selling information that do not involve company promotional materials.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of a product feature:
explanation: Soft material. A feature is a physical characteristic or quality of a product. It is something that the customer can touch, feel, smell, see, or measure. It helps to describe the product. Soft material is a feature because customers can see, feel, and touch it. For example, the material used to cover an automobile seat is a feature of the automobile seat. Easy to repair, inexpensive, and long-lasting are product benefits.

prompt: Which of the following are important components of an automobile's suspension and steering system:
explanation: Ball joints. A ball joint is a type of connection where a ball moves within a socket. Ball joints are important components of an automobile's suspension and steering system that enable steering and suspension parts to move. Piston rings, valve springs, and wire gauges are not components of the suspension and steering system.

prompt: The component of an automobile's fuel system that is used to keep the fuel clean is the fuel
explanation: Filter. A fuel filter is a straining device that removes foreign matter and dirt from the fuel. A fuel filter is an important component of an automobile's fuel system because an automobile operates more efficiently when the fuel is clean. A fuel pump pulls fuel from the fuel tank and forces it to the carburetor or injector pump. A fuel gauge indicates the amount of gasoline in the fuel tank.

prompt: Which of the following is part of an automobile engine's front-end construction:
explanation: Camshaft drive mechanism. This is part of the engine front-end assembly. The cylinder head and exhaust manifold are parts of the engine top end. The cylinder block is part of the engine bottom end.

prompt: What is a reason why selling brand name goods often is important to automotive businesses?
explanation: Customer recognition. A reason why many automotive businesses sell brand name goods is because customers recognize the brands. Selling brand name goods often is fairly easy because of national advertising that promotes the brand to all customers. Customers often associate brand names with quality and acceptability which makes it easier for salespeople to persuade them to buy. Automotive businesses usually receive cooperation from all vendors regardless of the type of good. Automotive businesses (e.g., tire stores, auto parts stores) generally design their own displays unless they are using a type of point-of-purchase display. Financial leverage refers to an automotive business's economic condition.

prompt: Suggestion selling is a technique used in the selling process to
explanation: Reaffirm the buyer-seller relationship. The final phase in the selling process involves reaffirming the buyer-seller relationship. One technique that salespeople use to reaffirm the relationship is to use suggestion selling, which involves recommending complementary products. By suggesting other products salespeople are reassuring customers that their business is important. Before salespeople use suggestion selling, they prescribe solutions to problems, establish relationships with customers, and discover customers' needs.

prompt: "Don't you like the large amount of trunk space in this car?" is an example of a(n) __________ question.
explanation: Assumptive. The salesperson thinks s/he knows that the customer wants a lot of trunk space in a car, so s/he expects the customer to say "yes." Open-ended questions require more than a "yes" or "no" response. Interpretive questions require the questioner to summarize the respondent's comments in his/her own words. This question is specific rather than general.

prompt: Identify the method of handling objections in the following situation: Customer: "I don't think I can replace these windshield wipers by myself." Salesperson: "Do you know Mrs. Johnson who lives on your street?" Customer: "Yes, I do." Salesperson: "Well, she has the same car model that you do and she told me that the process was very easy."
explanation: Testimonial. The testimonial is a method of handling objections in which the salesperson uses a neutral third party who has tried the product as an example. In an inquiry, questions are asked to enable customers to answer their own objections. The point-counterpoint method allows the salesperson to agree on a customer's valid point and then answer the point by offering an equal or superior point. Toss-it-back is designed to turn the customer's objection into a valid reason for buying.

prompt: A customer who is purchasing a battery is paying cash. Which of the following is the second step that an auto-parts store cashier takes in processing the sale?
choices: Ring up the transaction to determine the total amount of the sale
Ask to see the customer's driver's license
Receive and verify the cash amount from the customer
Present the total of the sale to the customer
explanation: Present the total of the sale to the customer. The first step is ringing the transaction on the cash register to determine the total amount of the sale, which would include any taxes. The second step is to tell the customer the total amount of the sale. The third step is receiving and verifying the cash from the customer. A cash transaction for a battery does not require a customer to provide any form of identification. An identification card is usually required when purchasing items with a credit card or check as a safety precaution to protect the customer and business from credit-card/check theft.

prompt: What is a mark on goods that automotive accessory store cashiers often scan in order to enter the selling price into the computer system?
explanation: UPC. The Universal Product Code (UPC) is a label encoded with product information such as price, brand, size, etc., to be read by an electronic scanner. Automotive accessory store cashiers using a computerized point-of-sale system use a scanner to read the information on the UPC bar code. The scanner records the information into the computer system, which reports the selling price and subtracts the item from inventory. POS is a point-of-sale terminal. FOB (free on board) is a shipping term. GDP is gross domestic product.

prompt: What is the set amount of money that muffler shops place in the cash register at the beginning of each business day?
explanation: Change fund. The change fund is the money placed in the cash drawer at the beginning of each work day or shift to enable muffler shop employees to make change easily. The cash drawer is the part of the cash register in which money is stored. Small change and pocket money are terms for the small amounts of cash that some people carry with them at all times.

prompt: How much refund is due a customer who returns a cash purchase that cost $39.95 plus sales tax of 5.5%?
explanation: $42.15. The entire amount of the sale should be refunded to the customer who returns a cash purchase. In this case, the sales tax should be calculated and added to the purchase amount to determine the amount of the refund ($39.95 x 5.5% or .055 = $2.197 or $2.20; $39.95 + $2.20 = $42.15).

prompt: What does an employee of an automotive repair business usually look up when preparing a service order?
explanation: Cost of parts. When employees prepare service orders, they usually look up the cost of the parts that will be required to repair the automobile. In many cases, the repair requires replacing a part that has malfunctioned. Employees can look up the price of parts in a parts catalog and write the amount on the service order. This is an important step because customers want to know the price of the parts as well as an estimate of the labor costs involved in repairing their automobiles. Employees do not look up the names of customers or the type of vehicle because this information is provided by the customers. Customers usually explain the type of problems they are having with their vehicles when they bring them in for repair.
